lines.watchItem: Merchant-GPU demand is running well ahead of supply, with NVIDIA setting data-center revenue records and hyperscalers lifting 2026 spending by more than 70%. Wafer-start planning at the leading nodes is exposed to whether this booked demand holds as capacity comes online.

Packaging capacity stays fully booked through 2027 but its shortfall is closing, while scarce high-bandwidth memory has become the tighter limit on how much GPU output can actually ship. The binding constraint on realizable revenue is moving from packaging toward memory supply.

Custom accelerators from hyperscalers are growing faster than merchant GPUs, a new design like Anthropic's is being explored on a 2-nanometer process, and AMD keeps adding its own merchant wins. The leading-node customer base is widening from a few merchant vendors toward a broader mix of in-house silicon.

End-market GPU prices stay firm, with NVIDIA holding a 75% gross margin and TSMC's margin up more than nine points, as broadening AI demand tightens capacity and lifts foundry pricing power. Pricing power across the value chain is exposed to how long this supply tightness lasts.

Policy and second-source moves are stacking up: NVIDIA's China sales more than halved under export limits, Chinese labs are training on tens of thousands of domestic non-NVIDIA chips, and Intel and Samsung are pressing their own foundry offers. These shifts bear on where AI foundry demand lands and the exposure around it.
